findings.summary: Recheck of #53 confirms the incoming-deletion defect is fixed correctly and fail-closed: apply_domain_delta now refuses any incoming tombstone that still has a live target identity (migration.py:87-89) before any table replacement, while locks on all domain tables plus the manifest recheck at line 78 are taken first, and the tombstone's lack of a pre-deletion digest is explicitly reasoned about so no baseline-equality guess is made. The new test (tests/test_pai_migration.py:96-113) recreates a concrete restored target at version 2, deletes only in the source baseline, imports with the exact current manifest, and asserts the conflict and no-erasure state. Retained target tombstones still apply after replacement via delete_derived_in and cannot be reset by re-import (test_repeated_domain_import...). Deletion is itself bounded (128-node graph, lineage advisory lock), integrity-checks payloads before destructive writes, and scrubbed notifications/artifacts preserve privacy. Unknown pricing/confirmations remain monotone and un-retried; no P0 or P1 remains.
